newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germany's Lafontaine wants elections after gold row.
newsitem.headline: Germany's Lafontaine wants elections after gold row.

text.p: Oskar Lafontaine, the leader of Germany's opposition Social Democrats (SPD), urged Chancellor Helmut Kohl to call a general election, saying the government's plan to revalue gold reserves was damaging Bonn's credibility.

Lafontaine told the news magazine Der Spiegel that Kohl's centre-right coalition was now having to resort to creative accounting to meet the criteria for European monetary union (EMU) and was incapable of producing solid budgets.

"The economic and finance policies of the Kohl government have failed. The coalition is so split it's not capable of acting. It would be good for Germany if it cleared the path for fresh elections," Lafontaine said in the interview released on Saturday.

Germany's central bank, the Bundesbank, has rejected Finance Minister Theo Waigel's plan to revalue its gold and currency reserves this year and use the booked profit to retire debt. Waigel has vowed to stick to the plan.
"The international reaction to the government's gold plans has been catastrophic," Lafontaine said in the interview to be published in Monday's edition of the news weekly.
"It's embarrassing that the coalition now wants to do the sort of accounting tricks for which it's always reproached others," he said.
